text_blocks: When picking pizza in New York, check the crust style (thin, Sicilian, grandma) and whether the shop sells by the slice. Many top-rated spots cluster near subway stations.
Cash-only counters still exist, so check payment options before queuing during peak hours.

related_questions.question: Do NYC pizza shops sell by the slice? (mock)
related_questions.snippet: Most do. Whole pies are often a better deal for groups of three or more.

related_questions.question: Which shops stay open late? (mock)
related_questions.snippet: Several East Village and Midtown counters serve until 2am or later.

related_questions.question: How long are the lines? (mock)
related_questions.snippet: Expect 20-45 minutes at peak; weekday lunch is usually quieter.

related_questions.question: Any vegan-friendly pizza spots? (mock)
related_questions.snippet: Yes — dairy-free pies are now common across Manhattan and Brooklyn.
